correctness.rationale: For complex Haar x on the n-sphere, E|<Rx,x>|²=(tr RR*+|tr R|²)/(n(n+1)). Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonality to span_C{I,A,A*} makes the stated distance bound the exact best affine L² error. With normal A=Σλ_j P_j, block-Haar symmetry yields E[<Bx,x>|T]=Σ T_j tr(BP_j)/rank P_j with Dirichlet positive block masses; affine-independent distinct λ_j (at most three noncollinear planar vertices) uniquely recover all T_j from Z=Σλ_jT_j, hence this predictor is affine in Z and Zbar and is the nonlinear conditional expectation. Conversely, if every spectral projector has affine conditional mean, at extreme spectral vertices it tends to Kronecker boundary values; for ≥3 collinear distinct λ, a nonextreme spectral value gives an affine function zero at both segment ends but positive mean, and for non-simplex polygons a nonextreme λ or ≥4 extreme vertices forces an affine function zero at three noncollinear vertices but positive mean. Thus an actual spectral projection strictly beats affine regression. The exact n=3 symmetric Dirichlet joint density gives predictor (1-|t|)/2, conditional variance E=1/24, affine residual 1/18. No claim for nonnormal/infinite-dimensional operators.
